capsuleTopic.title: Faith
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Trust · belief · testimony · action · endurance · faithfulness
capsuleTopic.orientation: Trace faith without forcing one definition onto every Scene: trust before an outcome, belief after testimony or signs, loyalty under pressure, faith expressed through action and love, and “the faith” handed to a community.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow who trusts or refuses, what word, person, sign, or promise receives confidence, what action follows, and what the source leaves unresolved.

passages.title: Hezekiah trusts unlike the kings around him

passages.title: Trust does good while waiting

passages.observation: The teacher joins wholehearted trust with acknowledging God, refusing self-wisdom, fearing the LORD, and turning from evil.

passages.observation: The greedy person stirs conflict, the one who trusts the LORD prospers, and the one who trusts his own heart is called a fool.

passages.excerpt: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the LORD is kept safe.
passages.observation: The proverb contrasts fear of human beings with safety in trusting the LORD.

passages.observation: As Judah fears an alliance against it, Isaiah tells Ahaz not to fear and warns that without belief he will not be established.

passages.title: Two kinds of trust become two kinds of tree

passages.title: A centurion sends others to speak for him

passages.title: A woman and a father hear words of faith

nodes.note: The three refuse the image, say God can rescue them, and also refuse worship if he does not; a fourth figure appears in the furnace.
nodes.title: Three exiles trust God without controlling the outcome

nodes.note: Those thought destroyed are described as at peace, tested like gold, and remaining faithful in love.
nodes.title: The faithful dead are held in God’s hand

nodes.note: The mother recalls Abraham and Daniel’s companions as she urges her sons to endure rather than abandon the law.
nodes.title: A mother strengthens seven sons through ancestral memory

nodes.note: Concerned that affliction might undo the community, Paul sends Timothy, receives news of faith and love, and prays to supply what is lacking.
nodes.title: Paul sends Timothy to learn whether faith endured

nodes.note: The community is urged to draw near in full assurance, hold hope, remember earlier endurance, and not shrink back.
nodes.title: Confidence must endure after costly public suffering

nodes.note: The chapter moves through creation, Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Israel, judges, kings, prophets, victories, losses, torture, and unreceived promises.
nodes.title: Faith remembers promises before fulfillment

nodes.note: Believers love and trust an unseen Jesus, endure tested faith, hope for grace, and are called to holiness and reverent conduct.
nodes.title: Unseen trust rejoices under testing

nodes.note: The poor and afflicted church is told not to fear coming suffering and to remain faithful to death for the crown of life.
nodes.title: Smyrna is called faithful to death

nodes.note: The beast receives authority, wages war on the saints, and the vision pauses to call for the endurance and faith of the saints.
nodes.title: Captivity and violence call for endurance and faith

payload.title: faith through endurance and death

payload.description: Inspect whose faith is named, when it is seen, whether it belongs to one person or a group, and what follows.

nodes.note: Jesus sees their faith, pronounces forgiveness, answers accusations, and heals the man so the crowd can see his authority.
nodes.title: Jesus sees the faith of people carrying a paralytic

nodes.note: A leader asks for his dead daughter, a woman touches Jesus, and blind men answer that they believe he can heal them.
nodes.title: A leader, a bleeding woman, and two blind men approach

nodes.note: Friends lower a paralytic through the roof; Jesus sees their faith, pronounces forgiveness, and heals amid scribal objection.
nodes.title: A roof opens above Jesus

nodes.note: A woman touches Jesus and is told her faith has made her well; Jairus is told not to fear but believe after news of his daughter’s death.
nodes.title: Faith is named between long illness and sudden death

nodes.note: Though rebuked, Bartimaeus calls louder, names what he wants, receives sight, and follows Jesus on the way.
nodes.title: Bartimaeus keeps calling from the roadside

nodes.note: Ten people with skin disease are cleansed while going, but only a Samaritan returns to thank God and hears that his faith has made him well.
nodes.title: One healed man returns and is called faithful

nodes.note: A man unable to walk is healed at the temple, and Peter denies that personal power caused it, naming Jesus’ name and faith through him.
nodes.title: Peter attributes healing to faith in Jesus’ name

nodes.note: Paul sees that a man has faith to be healed, refuses pagan sacrifice, then strengthens disciples to continue in faith through many afflictions.
nodes.title: A healed man and new disciples enter suffering

payload.title: faith around healing

payload.description: Hold great faith, little faith, missing faith, mixed belief, and persistent appeal together.

nodes.note: A Gentile officer asks for healing, refuses to presume on Jesus’ presence, and reasons from authority; Jesus marvels at his faith.
nodes.title: A centurion trusts Jesus’ word at a distance

nodes.note: A storm covers the boat, the disciples wake Jesus, and he questions their fear before calming wind and sea.
nodes.title: Fear in the boat is called little faith

nodes.note: Peter answers Jesus’ command to come on the water, becomes afraid, cries out, and is caught as Jesus asks why he doubted.
nodes.title: Peter walks, fears, sinks, and is rescued

nodes.note: A woman cries for her daughter, receives silence and a hard exchange, answers with the children’s crumbs, and is praised for great faith.
nodes.title: A Canaanite woman persists through refusal

nodes.note: A father brings his suffering son after the disciples fail, Jesus heals him, and explains their inability in terms of little faith.
nodes.title: The disciples cannot heal a child

nodes.note: The disciples wake Jesus with an accusation of neglect; after calming the storm, he asks why they are afraid and whether they still have no faith.
nodes.title: The storm exposes fear and missing faith

nodes.note: The father tells the child’s history, asks if Jesus can help, then answers the call to believe with a cry that joins belief and unbelief.
nodes.title: A father believes and asks help for unbelief

payload.title: Jesus’ descriptions of faith

payload.description: Observe how reports, public speech, Scripture explanation, household hearing, and apostolic witness become grounds for belief.

nodes.note: Rahab hides the spies, confesses what Jericho has heard about the LORD, asks for household mercy, and marks her window.
nodes.title: Rahab acts on what she has heard

nodes.note: On the road to Emmaus, the risen Jesus hears disappointed hopes, calls the travelers slow to believe, interprets Scripture, and is recognized at the meal.
nodes.title: Two disciples are slow to believe the prophets

nodes.note: Many Samaritans believe first through the woman and then through Jesus’ word; an official believes Jesus’ promise before seeing his son healed.
nodes.title: Samaritans and a royal official believe through different paths

nodes.note: Philip explains Isaiah, announces Jesus, and the traveler asks for baptism before continuing with joy.
nodes.title: An Ethiopian official trusts the good news

nodes.note: Peter announces Jesus, forgiveness through believing in his name, and witness testimony; the Holy Spirit falls before the hearers are baptized.
nodes.title: Gentiles receive the Spirit while hearing

nodes.note: Paul announces forgiveness and justification, some reject the word, and Gentiles rejoice and believe as the message spreads.
nodes.title: Gentile hearers believe amid rejection

nodes.note: Paul speaks of the unknown God, Creator, repentance, judgment, and resurrection; some mock, some postpone, and some believe.
nodes.title: Athens divides over resurrection testimony

nodes.note: Paul holds Scripture passages together around Christ, the near word, heart belief, public confession, calling on the Lord, preaching, hearing, and Christ’s word.
nodes.title: Faith hears, confesses, and calls

payload.title: hearing, testimony, and response

payload.description: Distinguish the trust people exercise, the loyalty they embody, and the faithfulness attributed to God and Jesus.

nodes.note: The song describes a well-fed people who reject God, turn to other gods, and become children in whom there is no faithfulness.
nodes.title: An unfaithful generation abandons its maker

nodes.note: The speaker recalls being lifted from a pit, receives a new song, calls the trusting person blessed, and refuses to hide God’s faithfulness.
nodes.title: Waiting becomes public testimony

nodes.note: A trustworthy saying joins death and life, endurance and reign, denial and denial, then says God remains faithful because he cannot deny himself.
nodes.title: Faithlessness meets God’s faithfulness

nodes.note: Hebrews calls Jesus faithful over God’s house, quotes the wilderness warning, and says the generation could not enter because of unbelief.
nodes.title: Jesus is faithful while the wilderness generation is unbelieving

nodes.note: Heaven opens to a rider called Faithful and True who judges, bears hidden and public names, and is followed by heaven’s armies.
nodes.title: The rider is named Faithful and True

payload.title: human faith and divine faithfulness

payload.description: Trace testimony, signs, Jesus’ word, hidden belief, public confession, sight, and the Gospel’s written purpose.

nodes.note: The Word comes to his own, is not received by many, and gives God’s children authority to those who receive and believe his name.
nodes.title: Receiving the light is described as believing his name

nodes.note: Jesus changes water into wine at Cana, reveals his glory, and his disciples believe in him.
nodes.title: The first sign leads disciples to believe

nodes.note: Many Samaritans believe first through the woman and then through Jesus’ word; an official believes Jesus’ promise before seeing his son healed.
nodes.title: Samaritans and a royal official believe through different paths

nodes.note: After the feeding, Jesus tells the crowd that God’s work is to believe in the one he sent and speaks of coming, seeing, believing, and life.
nodes.title: The crowd asks what work God requires

nodes.note: After being expelled, the formerly blind man meets Jesus, asks who the Son of God is, believes, and worships while sight and blindness become disputed terms.
nodes.title: The healed man comes to believe amid investigation

nodes.note: Martha confesses Jesus as Christ and Son of God while grieving, and Jesus calls Lazarus from the tomb after asking whether she believes.
nodes.title: Martha believes before Lazarus comes out

nodes.note: John says many still do not believe despite signs, interprets this through Isaiah, and notes rulers who believe but fear public confession.
nodes.title: Many signs do not produce public belief

nodes.note: Thomas refuses the others’ report without physical evidence, meets the risen Jesus, confesses, and is followed by a blessing on those who do not see yet believe.
nodes.title: Thomas asks to see, then confesses

payload.title: believing in John

payload.description: Listen for fear, waiting, refuge, envy, tears, social pressure, and praise rather than extracting one mood.

nodes.note: The speaker moves from distress and public challenge to sacrifice, trust, gladness, and sleep in safety.
nodes.title: Trust settles into sleep

nodes.note: The speaker names fear, seeks God’s face, asks not to be abandoned, and ends by telling the heart to wait courageously.
nodes.title: Confidence and waiting share one song

nodes.note: The speaker takes refuge, entrusts his spirit, laments isolation, and calls others to courage after receiving mercy.
nodes.title: Trust speaks from a closing net

nodes.note: The poem answers envy with trust, doing good, delight, committed ways, stillness, patience, and refusal of anger.
nodes.title: Trust does good while waiting

nodes.note: God is refuge amid cosmic collapse, war, and political uproar; the city is sustained and the nations are told to be still.
nodes.title: Refuge remains when earth and nations shake

nodes.note: Surrounded by attackers, the speaker admits fear, chooses trust, repeats confidence, and remembers tears before rescue is complete.
nodes.title: Fear and trust are spoken in the same breath

nodes.note: The speaker calls God rock and refuge, warns against status and wealth, and tells the people to pour out their hearts.
nodes.title: Silence waits for God alone

nodes.note: The speaker nearly slips over the prosperity of the wicked, enters God’s sanctuary, and ends by making God his refuge.
nodes.title: Faithfulness survives envy and confusion

nodes.note: The speaker names shelter, rescue, angelic guarding, and divine answer for the one who holds fast to God.
nodes.title: Refuge language reaches its strongest claims

payload.title: the voices of trust

payload.description: Keep Genesis, Habakkuk, Romans, Galatians, and James in their distinct arguments.

nodes.note: Abram names his childlessness, receives a promise as numerous as the stars, and believes the LORD, who counts it as righteousness.
nodes.title: Abram believes the promise

nodes.note: The prophet waits, receives a vision for an appointed time, and hears a contrast between the proud person and the righteous who lives by faithfulness.
nodes.title: The righteous person lives by faithfulness

nodes.note: Paul calls the gospel God’s power for salvation and says God’s righteousness is revealed from faith to faith before quoting Habakkuk.
nodes.title: The gospel reveals righteousness from faith to faith

nodes.note: Paul describes righteousness through faith in Jesus Christ, redemption in Christ, exclusion of boasting, and one God who justifies Jew and Gentile by faith.
nodes.title: Faith and boasting meet God’s righteousness

nodes.note: Paul reads Genesis 15, David’s blessing, circumcision, promise, Abraham’s body, and resurrection faith inside one argument about reckoning.
nodes.title: Abraham is counted righteous before circumcision

nodes.note: Paul says a person is not justified by works of law but through faith in Jesus Christ, then speaks of union with Christ and grace.
nodes.title: Paul opposes justification by works of law

nodes.note: Paul asks how the Galatians received the Spirit, cites Abraham’s belief, contrasts law and faith, and quotes Habakkuk before naming blessing for the nations.
nodes.title: Abraham, Spirit, curse, and Habakkuk meet in one argument

nodes.note: James challenges a claim to faith that withholds material care, invokes demons’ belief, and reads Abraham and Rahab through enacted trust.
nodes.title: Faith without works is called dead

payload.title: faith and righteousness

payload.description: Inspect when signs lead to belief, fail to sustain it, answer a request, or become an attempted test of God.

nodes.note: Moses expects disbelief, and God gives signs so Israel may believe that the God of the ancestors has appeared to him.
nodes.title: Moses asks what will make Israel believe

nodes.note: Aaron speaks the LORD’s words and performs the signs; the people believe, hear that God has seen their suffering, and bow in worship.
nodes.title: Israel believes the report

nodes.note: Israel sees Egypt defeated, fears the LORD, and believes in the LORD and in Moses after passing through the sea.
nodes.title: Israel believes after the sea

nodes.note: Israel wants to return to Egypt, Joshua and Caleb urge trust in the LORD, and God asks how long the people will not believe despite the signs.
nodes.title: The wilderness generation refuses to believe

nodes.note: Jesus changes water into wine at Cana, reveals his glory, and his disciples believe in him.
nodes.title: The first sign leads disciples to believe

nodes.note: Many Samaritans believe first through the woman and then through Jesus’ word; an official believes Jesus’ promise before seeing his son healed.
nodes.title: Samaritans and a royal official believe through different paths

nodes.note: John says many still do not believe despite signs, interprets this through Isaiah, and notes rulers who believe but fear public confession.
nodes.title: Many signs do not produce public belief

nodes.note: Thomas refuses the others’ report without physical evidence, meets the risen Jesus, confesses, and is followed by a blessing on those who do not see yet believe.
nodes.title: Thomas asks to see, then confesses

payload.title: signs and belief

payload.description: Notice where faith names shared teaching, community identity, inheritance, or something guarded and defended.

nodes.note: Paul calls the community to stand in one spirit for the faith of the gospel, without intimidation, while sharing the conflict and suffering.
nodes.title: One faith is contested under suffering

nodes.note: The letter aims at love from a pure heart, good conscience, and sincere faith, then names people who have rejected conscience and wrecked their faith.
nodes.title: Sincere faith is contrasted with speculation and shipwreck

nodes.note: Timothy is told to reject myths, train in godliness, model speech and conduct, attend to teaching, and persist.
nodes.title: The minister is trained in the words of faith

nodes.note: Paul recalls Timothy’s sincere faith in Lois and Eunice, urges courage, and tells him to guard the entrusted good through the Spirit.
nodes.title: Faith is remembered across generations and guarded as a deposit

nodes.note: Paul writes for the faith of God’s chosen and knowledge of truth, calls Titus a true child in a common faith, and requires leaders to hold the trustworthy word.
nodes.title: Shared faith and trustworthy teaching frame leadership

nodes.note: Jude urges readers to contend for the faith once delivered, remembers examples of rebellion, and tells the beloved to build themselves up in faith and mercy.
nodes.title: The faith is something entrusted and defended

payload.title: faith as an entrusted body of teaching

payload.description: Compare practiced preparation, prayer, public speech, refusal, and confidence where outcomes are not yet visible.

nodes.note: David refuses Saul’s armor, recalls prior deliverance, and goes against Goliath declaring that the battle belongs to the LORD.
nodes.title: David faces Goliath in the LORD’s name

nodes.note: Under Assyrian threat, Hezekiah seeks Isaiah, lays the letter before God, prays, and receives deliverance without fighting the siege himself.
nodes.title: Hezekiah spreads the threat before the LORD

nodes.note: Jehoshaphat confesses that Judah has no power and does not know what to do, then calls the people to believe the LORD and his prophets.
nodes.title: Judah stands still before a larger army

nodes.note: The three refuse the image, say God can rescue them, and also refuse worship if he does not; a fourth figure appears in the furnace.
nodes.title: Three exiles trust God without controlling the outcome

nodes.note: Daniel continues his established prayers, is thrown to the lions, and is found unharmed because he trusted his God.
nodes.title: Daniel keeps praying under a death decree

nodes.note: Surrounded by attackers, the speaker admits fear, chooses trust, repeats confidence, and remembers tears before rescue is complete.
nodes.title: Fear and trust are spoken in the same breath

payload.title: trust under threat

payload.description: Keep deliverance, complaint, refusal, public failure, memory, and later warning in sequence.

nodes.note: Israel sees Egypt defeated, fears the LORD, and believes in the LORD and in Moses after passing through the sea.
nodes.title: Israel believes after the sea

nodes.note: Israel wants to return to Egypt, Joshua and Caleb urge trust in the LORD, and God asks how long the people will not believe despite the signs.
nodes.title: The wilderness generation refuses to believe

nodes.note: Moses strikes the rock after God commanded speech, and God says Moses and Aaron did not believe him so as to honor him before Israel.
nodes.title: Moses and Aaron fail to trust at Meribah

nodes.note: Moses recalls the spies, the people’s fear, and their refusal to go up even after he says that God will fight for them.
nodes.title: Israel does not believe the promise of the land

nodes.note: Moses recalls the command to possess the land, says Israel did not believe or listen, and appeals to God’s redemption and promise.
nodes.title: Kadesh is remembered as rebellion and unbelief

nodes.note: Hebrews calls Jesus faithful over God’s house, quotes the wilderness warning, and says the generation could not enter because of unbelief.
nodes.title: Jesus is faithful while the wilderness generation is unbelieving

nodes.note: Hebrews says a promise of rest remains, warns that the message did not benefit earlier hearers, and urges entry while God’s word exposes the heart.
nodes.title: Good news can be heard without being joined by faith

payload.title: wilderness belief and refusal

payload.description: Trace how grace, action, care, love, and formation challenge both boasting and empty profession.

nodes.note: Paul tells the community to receive the weak in faith, restrain judgment, act before the Lord, and avoid actions not proceeding from faith.
nodes.title: Believers disagree over food and days

nodes.note: Paul imagines extraordinary speech, knowledge, generosity, suffering, and all faith, then says they amount to nothing without love.
nodes.title: Faith that moves mountains can still lack love

nodes.note: Paul warns against taking circumcision as the basis of justification and says what counts in Christ is faith working through love.
nodes.title: Faith works through love

nodes.note: The letter moves from death and hostile powers to mercy, shared life with Christ, salvation by grace through faith, and a life prepared for good works.
nodes.title: Salvation by grace through faith leads to good works

nodes.note: Paul remembers work of faith, labor of love, and patience of hope as the Thessalonians turn from idols and wait for Jesus.
nodes.title: Faith works while a community waits

nodes.note: James challenges a claim to faith that withholds material care, invokes demons’ belief, and reads Abraham and Rahab through enacted trust.
nodes.title: Faith without works is called dead

nodes.note: The letter addresses those who received equally precious faith and urges them to supply virtue, knowledge, self-control, endurance, godliness, affection, and love.
nodes.title: Faith is supplied with practiced qualities

payload.title: faith into works and love
